svg.text: Juice Shop · 20.0.0 · 8 components · 17 data flows · 4 trust boundaries (2 inferred) · 57 threats

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-01; tb-2 External → C-02; tb-5 External → C-08
Trust boundary crossing: tb-4 C-01 → External
df-001: Browser requests Angular SPA static assets (HTML, JS bundles) served by Express static middleware (HTTP)

df-002: POST /rest/user/login - user submits email and password; handler issues JWT on success (HTTP) df-002 authentication: email and password submitted in JSON request body; no prior session required; evidence: routes/login.ts:18

df-003: POST /rest/2fa/status or TOTP verify - second-factor TOTP code submitted after credential check (HTTP) df-003 authentication: TOTP code in request body following password-based first factor; interim token carried from login step; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:31
df-004: POST /api/Users - self-registration, no authentication required (HTTP) df-004 authentication: registration endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests; evidence: server.ts:407

df-005: Angular SPA API calls to authenticated REST endpoints; HTTP interceptor attaches Bearer JWT from localStorage (HTTP) df-005 authentication: JWT retrieved from localStorage and set in Authorization header by request.interceptor.ts; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13

df-006: Angular SPA calls to unauthenticated public REST endpoints (product listing, challenge status, configuration) (HTTP) df-007: Angular SPA calls to authenticated REST endpoints — alternative using cookie-based session (data erasure flow) (HTTP) df-006 authentication: public endpoints such as GET /api/Products and GET /rest/admin/application-configuration require no authentication; evidence: server.ts:605 df-006 access group: REST API auth variants; alternatives; step n/a df-007 authentication: session cookie checked in dataErasure.ts handler for GDPR data-erasure route; evidence: routes/dataErasure.ts:76 df-007 access group: REST API auth variants; alternatives; step n/a

df-008: Socket.IO WebSocket connection for real-time challenge notifications and score updates (WebSocket) df-008 authentication: no authentication check found in Socket.IO event registration; transport-level auth not verified; evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:24

df-009: Sequelize ORM query to SQLite: user lookup by email for login credential verification (SQL) df-009 authentication: in-process SQLite accessed via Sequelize ORM; no network authentication; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-010: Sequelize ORM reads/writes to SQLite for all application data (users, orders, products, baskets, payments) (SQL) df-010 authentication: in-process SQLite file accessed via Sequelize; no network authentication layer; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-011: MarsDB in-process reads/writes for product reviews (posts collection) and orders collection (in-process) df-011 authentication: MarsDB is an in-process embedded store; no network transport or authentication; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-012: POST /rest/chat proxies user message to Ollama LLM or OpenAI-compatible endpoint for chatbot/hint generation (HTTP) df-012 authentication: Ollama local API at port 11434 has no authentication; OpenAI-compatible provider may use api-key not verified in code; evidence: lib/startup/validatePreconditions.ts:236
Internet Attacker → C-01 · Juice Shop API Server: scenario 1, 2, 4, 5; its findings also affect C-05 · MarsDB Embedded Document Store
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Authentication and Session Surface: scenario 1, 3, 5; its findings also affect C-01 · Juice Shop API Server
Internet Attacker → C-07 · Web3 / NFT Surface: scenario 2, 3, 5
Supply-Chain / Build Attacker → C-08 · CI/CD Pipeline: scenario 2, 3, 5
Internet Attacker → C-06 · Socket.IO Real-Time WebSocket Channel: scenario 5
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:61 (reported finding)
Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:83 (reported finding); Server-side templates — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:87 (reported finding)

g.title: Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth Authorization Server df-013: Browser redirect to Google OAuth authorization endpoint using implicit flow (response_type=token, no state parameter) (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit flow initiated from login component; response_type=token; state parameter absent df-014: Google redirects browser to /oauth with token in URL fragment; oauth.component.ts derives credentials from email (HTTPS); Access token delivered in URL fragment to /oauth callback route; token then used to derive Juice Shop credentials df-015: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

C-03 · Angular SPA Frontend df-013: Browser redirect to Google OAuth authorization endpoint using implicit flow (response_type=token, no state parameter) (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit flow initiated from login component; response_type=token; state parameter absent df-014: Google redirects browser to /oauth with token in URL fragment; oauth.component.ts derives credentials from email (HTTPS); Access token delivered in URL fragment to /oauth callback route; token then used to derive Juice Shop credentials df-015: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
asset badges require linked findings and evidenced storage
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
Username eval gives server code execution
Stored XSS steals browser session tokens

The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.

interim token carried from login step

Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
